The handler's filter only excludes emails matching existing booking.attendees and blacklisted entries, so duplicate emails within a single direct/replayed mutation pass through and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee rows, which are also propagated to calendar/email payloads. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, `uniqueGuests` is created by filtering out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees`, but it does NOT deduplicate the input `guests` array itself. If a client sends `guests: ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`, both will pass the filter (since neither is in existing attendees yet) and both will be created via `createMany`. The schema in addGuests.schema.ts is just `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness validation. This would create duplicate attendee records and send duplicate calendar invites.
